comparison.name: XML
comparison.description: The XML InfoSets should be canonicalized and compared.

comparison.name: Fragment
comparison.description: A 'fragment' refers to an XML based instance which has multiple top-level elements and NO XML declaration. The comparator for this should simply wrap the entire fragment in a container element and perform XML comparison.

comparison.name: Text
comparison.description: Each line of non-whitespace text should match. New-line sequences may vary and should be neutralized. Due to issues with the XML serialization of certain characters (e.g. '<'), it is not possible to simply compare the actual and expected results. Rather (as is the case with the 'Fragment' comparator) the test harness should convert the results into valid XML (by adding a container element) and perform comparison on the XML canonicalized versions of the results.

comparison.name: Ignore
comparison.description: Only the presence/absence of this file is significant, not its content.

comparison.name: Inspect
comparison.description: Automated comparison is not possible. the output should be inspected by a human.

role.name: principal-data
role.description: This is the source that is handed in to the processor as the initial input sequence, setting the "evaluation context" as described in XQuery chapter 2.

role.name: supplemental-data
role.description: These are sources that may be read by functions such as fn:document() as the query is evaluated.

role.name: schema
role.description: These are schema definitions that may be referenced by sources or in the query.

role.name: dtd
role.description: These are dtd definitions that may be referenced by sources or in the query.

role.name: principal
role.description: This is an output (either text or XML) that will contain the query results. If the processor invocation sequence accepts a filename for results, this name may be passed, possibly prefixed by a partial directory path to allow storage of the results in a separate directory tree.

role.name: console-log
role.description: This is an output (text file tagged .log) that will contain the captured "console" output for a command-line invocation, or equivalent messages from a harness. The main goal is to capture error messages that came from the processor.
role.note: A test lab may choose to capture console output for every test case, in which case the presence of this element is a signal that the console log of this test contains messages that are significant to the pass/fail determination.

scenario.name: standard
scenario.description: A query this is expected to produce valid results. Principal input should always be specified, even if the query doesn't have any PathExpr.

scenario.name: parse-error
scenario.description: A query this is expected to raise a parsing/syntax error at query parse time. Principal input should always be specified, even if the query doesn't have any PathExpr.

scenario.name: runtime-error
scenario.description: A query this is expected to raise a runtime error at query parse time. Runtime errors in this case include those raised by static typing rules. Principal input should always be specified, even if the query doesn't have any PathExpr.

scenario.name: trivial
scenario.description: A query this is expected to produce valid results. Principal input should always be specified, even if the query doesn't have any PathExpr. The initial query returns an <xqx:xquery> element (Trivial Embedding of XQuery). This embedded query is then executed to produce the final result.

implementation-defined-item.name: expressionUnicode
implementation-defined-item.description: The version of Unicode that is used to construct expressions.

implementation-defined-item.name: collations
implementation-defined-item.description: The statically-known collations.

implementation-defined-item.name: implicitTimezone
implementation-defined-item.description: The implicit timezone.

implementation-defined-item.name: warningsMethod
implementation-defined-item.description: The circumstances in which warnings are raised, and the ways in which warnings are handled.

implementation-defined-item.name: errorsMethod
implementation-defined-item.description: The method by which errors are reported to the external processing environment.

implementation-defined-item.name: XMLVersion
implementation-defined-item.description: Whether the implementation is based on the rules of [XML 1.0] and [XML Names] or the rules of [XML 1.1] and [XML Names 1.1]. One of these sets of rules must be applied consistently by all aspects of the implementation.

implementation-defined-item.name: overwrittenContextComponents
implementation-defined-item.description: Any components of the static context or dynamic context that are overwritten or augmented by the implementation.

implementation-defined-item.name: axes
implementation-defined-item.description: Which of the optional axes are supported by the implementation, if the Full-Axis Feature is not supported.

implementation-defined-item.name: defaultOrderEmpty
implementation-defined-item.description: The default handling of empty sequences returned by an ordering key (sortspec) in an order by clause (empty least or empty greatest).

implementation-defined-item.name: pragmas
implementation-defined-item.description: The names and semantics of any extension expressions (pragmas) recognized by the implementation.

implementation-defined-item.name: optionDeclarations
implementation-defined-item.description: The names and semantics of any option declarations recognized by the implementation.

implementation-defined-item.name: externalFunctionProtocols
implementation-defined-item.description: Protocols (if any) by which parameters can be passed to an external function, and the result of the function can returned to the invoking query.

implementation-defined-item.name: moduleLocationHints
implementation-defined-item.description: The process by which the specific modules to be imported by a module import are identified, if the Module Feature is supported (includes processing of location hints, if any.)

implementation-defined-item.name: staticTypingExtensions
implementation-defined-item.description: Any static typing extensions supported by the implementation, if the Static Typing Feature is supported.

implementation-defined-item.name: serializationInvocation
implementation-defined-item.description: The means by which serialization is invoked, if the Serialization Feature is supported.

implementation-defined-item.name: serializationDefaults
implementation-defined-item.description: The default values for the byte-order-mark, encoding, media-type, normalization-form, omit-xml-declaration, standalone, and version parameters, if the Serialization Feature is supported.

implementation-defined-item.name: externalFunctionCall
implementation-defined-item.description: The result of an unsuccessful call to an external function (for example, if the function implementation cannot be found or does not return a value of the declared type).

implementation-defined-item.name: limits
implementation-defined-item.description: Limits on ranges of values for various data types, as enumerated in 5.3 Data Model Conformance.

implementation-defined-item.name: traceDestination
implementation-defined-item.description: The destination of the trace output is implementation-defined. See 4 The Trace Function.

implementation-defined-item.name: integerOperations
implementation-defined-item.description: For xs:integer operations, implementations that support limited-precision integer operations must either raise an error [err:FOAR0002] or provide an implementation-defined mechanism that allows users to choose between raising an error and returning a result that is modulo the largest representable integer value. See 6.2 Operators on Numeric Values.

implementation-defined-item.name: decimalDigits
implementation-defined-item.description: For xs:decimal values the number of digits of precision returned by the numeric operators is implementation-defined. See 6.2 Operators on Numeric Values. See also 17.1.3.3 Casting to xs:decimal and 17.1.3.4 Casting to xs:integer.

implementation-defined-item.name: roundOrTruncate
implementation-defined-item.description: If the number of digits in the result exceeds the number of digits that the implementation supports, the result is truncated or rounded in an implementation-defined manner. See 6.2 Operators on Numeric Values. See also 17.1.3.3 Casting to xs:decimal and 17.1.3.4 Casting to xs:integer.

implementation-defined-item.name: Unicode
implementation-defined-item.description: It is implementation-defined which version of Unicode is supported by the features defined in this specification, but it is recommended that the most recent version of Unicode be used. See 7.1 String Types.

implementation-defined-item.name: normalizationForms
implementation-defined-item.description: For 7.4.6 fn:normalize-unicode, conforming implementations must support normalization form "NFC" and may support normalization forms "NFD", "NFKC", "NFKD", "FULLY-NORMALIZED". They may also support other normalization forms with implementation-defined semantics.

implementation-defined-item.name: collationUnits
implementation-defined-item.description: The ability to decompose strings into collation units suitable for substring matching is an implementation-defined property of a collation. See 7.5 Functions Based on Substring Matching.

implementation-defined-item.name: secondsDigits
implementation-defined-item.description: All minimally conforming processors must support year values with a minimum of 4 digits (i.e., YYYY) and a minimum fractional second precision of 1 millisecond or three digits (i.e., s.sss). However, conforming processors may set larger implementation-defined limits on the maximum number of digits they support in these two situations. See 10.1.1 Limits and Precision.

implementation-defined-item.name: stringToDecimal
implementation-defined-item.description: The result of casting a string to xs:decimal, when the resulting value is not too large or too small but nevertheless has too many decimal digits to be accurately represented, is implementation-defined. See 17.1.1 Casting from xs:string and xs:untypedAtomic.

implementation-defined-item.name: docProcessing
implementation-defined-item.description: Various aspects of the processing provided by 15.5.4 fn:doc are implementation-defined. Implementations may provide external configuration options that allow any aspect of the processing to be controlled by the user.

implementation-defined-item.name: weakenStable
implementation-defined-item.description: The manner in which implementations provide options to weaken the stable characteristic of 15.5.6 fn:collection and 15.5.4 fn:doc are implementation-defined.

implementation-defined-item.name: additionalTypes
implementation-defined-item.description: Support for additional user-defined or implementation-defined types is implementation-defined. (See 2.6.1 Representation of Types)

implementation-defined-item.name: undefinedProperties
implementation-defined-item.description: Some typed values in the data model are undefined. Attempting to access an undefined property is always an error. Behavior in these cases is implementation-defined and the host language is responsible for determining the result. (See 5 Accessors)

implementation-defined-item.name: sequenceNormalization
implementation-defined-item.description: For any implementation-defined output method, it is implementation-defined whether sequence normalization process takes place. (See 2 Sequence Normalization)

implementation-defined-item.name: outputMethods
implementation-defined-item.description: If the namespace URI is non-null for the method serialization parameter, then the parameter specifies an implementation-defined output method. (See 3 Serialization Parameters)

implementation-defined-item.name: normalizationFormBehavior
implementation-defined-item.description: If the value of the normalization-form form parameter is not NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD, fully-normalized, or none then the meaning of the value and it's effect is implementation-defined. (See 4 Phases of Serialization)

implementation-defined-item.name: additionalParams
implementation-defined-item.description: The effect of additional serialization parameters on the output of the serializer, where the name of such a parameter must be namespace-qualified, is implementation-defined or implementation-dependent. The extent of this effect on the output must not override the provisions of this specification. (See 3 Serialization Parameters)

implementation-defined-item.name: encodingPhase
implementation-defined-item.description: The effect of providing an option that allows the encoding phase to be skipped, so that the result of serialization is a stream of Unicode characters, is implementation-defined. The serializer is not required to support such an option. (See 4 Phases of Serialization)

implementation-defined-item.name: CDATASerialization
implementation-defined-item.description: An serializer may provide an implementation-defined mechanism to place CDATA sections in the result tree. (See 5.1.4 XML Output Method: the cdata-section-elements Parameter)

GroupInfo.title: Axes
GroupInfo.description: Tests in this group focus on the axes named in XQuery 3.2.1.1 and the / and // step operators of 3.2.1. Abbreviated versions (@ vs. attribute::) are included. NodeTests are typically *, node(), or a name.

test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax - parent::node() - Selects the parent of the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-9
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax - descendant::empnum - Selects the "empnum" descendants of the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-12
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax - descendant-or-self::employee - Selects all the "employee" descendant of the context node (selects employee, if the context node is "employee").

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-13
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax - self::employee - Selects the context node, if it is an "employee" element, otherwise returns empty sequence. This test retuns an "employee" element.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-14
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax - self::hours - Selects the context node, if it is an "hours" element, otherwise returns empty sequence. This test retuns the empty sequence.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-15
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax child::employee/descendant:empnum- Selects the empnum element descendants of the employee element children of the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-16
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax child::*/child:pnum)- Selects the pnum grandchildren of the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-18
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate /descendant::pnum - Selects all the pnum elements in the same document as the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-19
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate /descendant::employee/child::pnum selects all the pnum elements that have an "employee" parent and that are in the same document as the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-20
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "child::employee[fn:position() = 1]". Selects the first employee child of the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-21
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "child::employee[fn:position() = fn:last()]". Selects the last "employee" child of the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-22
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "child::employee[fn:position() = fn:last()-1]. Selects the previous to the last one "employee" child of the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-23
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "child::hours[fn:position() > 1]". Selects all the para children of the context node other than the first "hours" child of the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-26
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "/descendant::employee[fn:position() = 12]". Selects the twelfth employee element in the document containing the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-27
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "/child::works/child::employee[fn:position() = 5]/child::hours[fn:position() = 2]". Selects the second "hours" of the fifth "employee" of the "works" whose parent is the document node that contains the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-28
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "child::employee[attribute::name eq "Jane Doe 11"]". Selects all "employee" children of the context node that have a "name" attribute with value "Jane Doe 11".

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-29
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "child::employee[attribute::gender eq 'female'][fn:position() = 5]". Selects the fifth employee child of the context node that has a gender attribute with value "female".

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-30
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "child::employee[child::empnum = 'E3']". Selects the employee children of the context node that have one or more empnum children whose typed value is equal to the string "E3".

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-31
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "child::employee[child::status]". Selects the employee children of the context node that have one or more status children.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-32
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "child::*[self::pnum or self::empnum]". Selects the pnum and empnum children of the context node.

test-case.name: unabbreviatedSyntax-33
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates unabbreviated syntax. Evaluate "child::*[self::empnum or self::pnum][fn:position() = fn:last()]". Selects the last empnum or pnum child of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-1
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "hours". Selects the "hours" element children of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-2
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "text()". Selects all text node children of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-3
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "@name". Selects the name attribute of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-5
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee[1]". Selects the first employee child of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-6
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "para[fn:last()]". Selects the last employee child of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-7
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "*/hours". Selects all hours grandchildren of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-8
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "/works/employee[5]/hours[2]". Selects the second hours of the fifth employee of the book whose parent is the document node that contains the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-9
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee//hours". Selects the hours element descendants of the employee element children of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-10
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "//hours". Selects all the hours descendants of the root document node and thus selects all hours elements in the same document as the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-12
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "//overtime/day". Selects all the day elements in the same document as the context node that have an overtime parent.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-13
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, ".//day". Selects the day element descendants of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-14
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "..". Selects the parent of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-16
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee[@name="Jane Doe 11"]". Selects all employee children of the context node that have a name attribute with a value "Jane Doe 11".

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-17
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee[@gender="female"][5]". Selects the fifth element child of the context node that has a gender attribute with value "female".

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-18
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee[5][@gender="female"]". Selects the fifth employee child of the context node if that child has a gender attribute with value "female".

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-19
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee[status="active"]". Selects the employee children of the context node that have one or more status children whose typed value is equal to the string "active".

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-20
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee[overtime]". Selects the employee children of the context node that have one or more overtime children.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-21
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee[@name and @type]". Selects all the employee children of the context node that have both a name attribute and a type attribute.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-22
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee/(status|overtime)/day". Selects every day element that has a parent that is either a status or an overime element, that in turn is a child of an employee element that is a child of the context node.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-24
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee/(status|overtime)/day". Selects every day element that has a parent that is either a status or an overime element, that in turn is a child of an employee element that is a child of the context node. Uses "union" Operator.

test-case.name: abbreviatedSyntax-25
test-case.Creator: Carmelo Montanez
test-case.description: Evaluates abbreviated syntax, "employee[@name=condition or @type=condition]". Selects all the employee children of the context node that have both a name attribute and a type attribute. Uses the "or" operator.

GroupInfo.title: Implicit Context
GroupInfo.description: Implementations are allowed to define an implicit context for their queries. What this means is that an XQuery expression can use the '.' or '/' axes without specifying any explicit context to bind these to. The binding of the implicit context to some input document is an implementation specific detail and should be handled by the individual test harness.

test-case.name: ST-PITest-01
test-case.Creator: Michael Dyck
test-case.description: In LetClause, binding expr's ST must be subtype of variable's ST. Under REC FS, both are 'processing-instruction?', so STA succeeds. Under PER FS, former is 'processing-instruction filesystem?', latter is 'processing-instruction filesytem', so STA fails, raises error. (Note that an implementation that doesn't do STA will not raise an error.)

test-case.name: ST-PITest-02
test-case.Creator: Michael Dyck
test-case.description: In LetClause, binding expr's ST must be subtype of variable's ST. Under REC FS, both are 'processing-instruction?', so STA succeeds. Under PER FS, former is 'processing-instruction nonexistent', latter is 'processing-instruction filesytem', so STA fails, raises error. (Note that an implementation that doesn't do STA will not raise an error, because the LetClause isn't evaluated.)

GroupInfo.title: Use Case "XMP": Experiences and Exemplars
GroupInfo.description: example queries that illustrate requirements gathered from the database and document communities.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q1
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List books published by Addison-Wesley after 1991, including their year and title.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q2
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Create a flat list of all the title-author pairs, with each pair enclosed in a "result" element.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q3
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For each book in the bibliography, list the title and authors, grouped inside a "result" element.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q4
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For each author in the bibliography, list the author's name and the titles of all books by that author, grouped inside a "result" element.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q5
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For each book found at both bstore1.example.com and bstore2.example.com, list the title of the book and its price from each source.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q6
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For each book that has at least one author, list the title and first two authors, and an empty "et-al" element if the book has additional authors.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q7
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List the titles and years of all books published by Addison-Wesley after 1991, in alphabetic order.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q8
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Find books in which the name of some element ends with the string "or" and the same element contains the string "Suciu" somewhere in its content. For each such book, return the title and the qualifying element.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q9
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: In the document "books.xml", find all section or chapter titles that contain the word "XML", regardless of the level of nesting.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q10
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: In the document "prices.xml", find the minimum price for each book, in the form of a "minprice" element with the book title as its title attribute.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q11
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For each book with an author, return the book with its title and authors. For each book with an editor, return a reference with the book title and the editor's affiliation.

test-case.name: xmp-queries-results-q12
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Find pairs of books that have different titles but the same set of authors (possibly in a different order).

GroupInfo.title: Use Case "TREE": Queries that preserve hierarchy
GroupInfo.description: An XML query language should have the ability to extract elements from documents while preserving their original hierarchy. This Use Case illustrates this requirement by means of a flexible document type named Book.

test-case.name: tree-queries-results-q1
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Prepare a (nested) table of contents for Book1, listing all the sections and their titles. Preserve the original attributes of each "section" element, if any.

test-case.name: tree-queries-results-q2
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Prepare a (flat) figure list for Book1, listing all the figures and their titles. Preserve the original attributes of each "figure" element, if any.

test-case.name: tree-queries-results-q3
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: How many sections are in Book1, and how many figures?

test-case.name: tree-queries-results-q4
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: How many top-level sections are in Book1?

test-case.name: tree-queries-results-q5
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Make a flat list of the section elements in Book1. In place of its original attributes, each section element should have two attributes, containing the title of the section and the number of figures immediately contained in the section.

test-case.name: tree-queries-results-q6
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Make a nested list of the section elements in Book1, preserving their original attributes and hierarchy. Inside each section element, include the title of the section and an element that includes the number of figures immediately contained in the section.

GroupInfo.title: Use Case "SEQ" - Queries based on Sequence
GroupInfo.description: Although sequence is not significant in most traditional database systems or object systems, it can be quite significant in structured documents. This use case presents a series of queries based on a medical report.

test-case.name: seq-queries-results-q1
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: In the Procedure section of Report1, what Instruments were used in the second Incision?

test-case.name: seq-queries-results-q2
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: In the Procedure section of Report1, what are the first two Instruments to be used?

test-case.name: seq-queries-results-q3
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: In Report1, what Instruments were used in the first two Actions after the second Incision?

test-case.name: seq-queries-results-q4
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: In Report1, find "Procedure" sections where no Anesthesia element occurs before the first Incision.

test-case.name: seq-queries-results-q5
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: In Report1, what happened between the first Incision and the second Incision?

GroupInfo.title: Use Case "R" - Access to Relational Data
GroupInfo.description: One important use of an XML query language will be to access data stored in relational databases. This use case describes one possible way in which this access might be accomplished.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q1
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List the item number and description of all bicycles that currently have an auction in progress, ordered by item number.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q2
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For all bicycles, list the item number, description, and highest bid (if any), ordered by item number.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q3
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Find cases where a user with a rating worse (alphabetically, greater) than "C" is offering an item with a reserve price of more than 1000.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q4
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List item numbers and descriptions of items that have no bids.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q5
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For bicycle(s) offered by Tom Jones that have received a bid, list the item number, description, highest bid, and name of the highest bidder, ordered by item number.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q6
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For each item whose highest bid is more than twice its reserve price, list the item number, description, reserve price, and highest bid.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q7
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Find the highest bid ever made for a bicycle or tricycle.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q8
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: How many items were actioned (auction ended) in March 1999?

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q9
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List the number of items auctioned each month in 1999 for which data is available, ordered by month.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q10
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For each item that has received a bid, list the item number, the highest bid, and the name of the highest bidder, ordered by item number.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q11
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List the item number and description of the item(s) that received the highest bid ever recorded, and the amount of that bid.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q12
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List the item number and description of the item(s) that received the largest number of bids, and the number of bids it (or they) received.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q13
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For each user who has placed a bid, give the userid, name, number of bids, and average bid, in order by userid.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q14
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List item numbers and average bids for items that have received three or more bids, in descending order by average bid.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q15
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List names of users who have placed multiple bids of at least $100 each.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q16
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List all registered users in order by userid; for each user, include the userid, name, and an indication of whether the user is active (has at least one bid on record) or inactive (has no bid on record).

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q17
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List the names of users, if any, who have bid on every item.

test-case.name: rdb-queries-results-q18
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List all users in alphabetic order by name. For each user, include descriptions of all the items (if any) that were bid on by that user, in alphabetic order.

GroupInfo.title: Use Case "SGML": Standard Generalized Markup Language
GroupInfo.description: The example document and queries in this Use Case were first created for a 1992 conference on Standard Generalized Markup Language (SGML).

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q1
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Locate all paragraphs in the report (all "para" elements occurring anywhere within the "report" element).

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q2
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Locate all paragraph elements in an introduction (all "para" elements directly contained within an "intro" element).

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q3
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Locate all paragraphs in the introduction of a section that is in a chapter that has no introduction (all "para" elements directly contained within an "intro" element directly contained in a "section" element directly contained in a "chapter" element. The "chapter" element must not directly contain an "intro" element).

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q4
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Locate the second paragraph in the third section in the second chapter (the second "para" element occurring in the third "section" element occurring in the second "chapter" element occurring in the "report").

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q5
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Locate all classified paragraphs (all "para" elements whose "security" attribute has the value "c").

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q6
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List the short titles of all sections (the values of the "shorttitle" attributes of all "section" elements, expressing each short title as the value of a new element.).

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q7
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Locate the initial letter of the initial paragraph of all introductions (the first character in the content [character content as well as element content] of the first "para" element contained in an "intro" element).

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q8a
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Locate all sections with a title that has "is SGML" in it. The string may occur anywhere in the descendants of the title element, and markup boundaries are ignored.

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q8b
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Same as (Q8a), but the string "is SGML" cannot be interrupted by sub-elements, and must appear in a single text node.

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q9
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Locate all the topics referenced by a cross-reference anywhere in the report (all the "topic" elements whose "topicid" attribute value is the same as an "xrefid" attribute value of any "xref" element).

test-case.name: sgml-queries-results-q10
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Locate the closest title preceding the cross-reference ("xref") element whose "xrefid" attribute is "top4" (the "title" element that would be touched last before this "xref" element when touching each element in document order).

GroupInfo.title: Use Case "STRING": String Search
GroupInfo.description: This use case is based on company profiles and a set of news documents which contain data for PR, mergers and acquisitions, etc. Given a company, the use case illustrates several different queries for searching text in news documents and different ways of providing query results by matching the information from the company profile and the content of the news items.

test-case.name: string-queries-results-q1
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Find the titles of all news items where the string "Foobar Corporation" appears in the title.

test-case.name: string-queries-results-q2
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Find news items where the Foobar Corporation and one or more of its partners are mentioned in the same paragraph and/or title. List each news item by its title and date.

test-case.name: string-queries-results-q4
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Find news items where a company and one of its partners is mentioned in the same news item and the news item is not authored by the company itself.

test-case.name: string-queries-results-q5
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: For each news item that is relevant to the Gorilla Corporation, create an "item summary" element. The content of the item summary is the content of the title, date, and first paragraph of the news item, separated by periods. A news item is relevant if the name of the company is mentioned anywhere within the content of the news item.

GroupInfo.title: Use Case "NS" - Queries Using Namespaces
GroupInfo.description: This use case is based on a scenario in which a neutral mediator is acting with public auction servers on behalf of clients. The reason for a client to use this imaginary service may be anonymity, better insurance, or the possibility to cover more than one market at a time.

test-case.name: ns-queries-results-q1
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List all unique namespaces used in the sample data.

test-case.name: ns-queries-results-q2
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Select the title of each record that is for sale.

test-case.name: ns-queries-results-q3
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Select all elements that have an attribute whose name is in the XML Schema namespace.

test-case.name: ns-queries-results-q4
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: List the target URI's of all XLinks in the document.

test-case.name: ns-queries-results-q5
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Select all records that have a remark in German.

test-case.name: ns-queries-results-q6
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Select the closing time elements of all AnyZone auctions currently monitored.

test-case.name: ns-queries-results-q7
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Select the homepage of all auctions where both seller and high bidder are registered at the same auctioneer.

test-case.name: ns-queries-results-q8
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Select all traders (either seller or high bidder) without negative comments.

GroupInfo.title: Use Case "PARTS" - Recursive Parts Explosion
GroupInfo.description: This use case is based on a "parts explosion" database that contains information about how parts are used in other parts.

test-case.name: parts-queries-results-q1
test-case.Creator: XML Query Group
test-case.description: Convert the sample document from "partlist" format to "parttree" format (see DTD section for definitions). In the result document, part containment is represented by containment of one "part" element inside another. Each part that is not part of any other part should appear as a separate top-level element in the output document.

GroupInfo.title: XMark -- An XML Benchmark
GroupInfo.description: This test suite group contains XMark, the XML Benchmark Project which was kindly donated to W3C's XQuery Test Suite. Frans Englich is marked as the creator of these tests and this is for the purpose of being able to locate the maintainer. The original author of these tests is the XML Benchmark team, see http://www.xml-benchmark.org/.

test-case.name: XMark-All
test-case.Creator: Frans Englich(maintainer, not original author)
test-case.description: Contains all the twenty XMark queries essentially concatenated with the comma operator, into one single query.

GroupInfo.title: FunctX -- A Collection Of Functions
GroupInfo.description: This test suite group contains FunctX, a collection of XQuery functions. They were written by Priscilla Walmsley, but is maintained by Frans Englich within the XQTS.
